A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a compact feature map for a polynomial kernel on the sphere, which is more accurate than the state of the art, and is applicable to a broader class of data than prior work.
we introduce SRF features for polynomial kernels and show that SRF features can be used for polynomial kernel learning on normalized data, which is a common setting for many applications.
SRF features provide a practical way to scale polynomial kernels to very large datasets, with a compact representation, low approximation error, and good classification accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of explicit feature map is a non-trivial problem that should be carefully considered for each kernel and application.
compactness of the feature map is not the only consideration when designing feature maps for kernel learning, and we provide a concrete example where a more compact map leads to worse performance.
the choice of feature map is not independent of the type of data being learned, but should be tailored to the specific data distribution.
